Class WorkoutDatabase

java.lang.Object
WorkoutDatabase
public class WorkoutDatabase extends Object
WorkoutDatabase.java The data layer for Phase 4. It connects to a SQLite database file that the user chooses and does every create, read, update and delete (CRUD) action with SQL, so the workouts now live in the database instead of in a list. The database has one table named workouts: workout_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY exercise_name TEXT duration_minutes INTEGER body_weight_lbs REAL met_value REAL completed INTEGER (1 = true, 0 = false, since SQLite has no boolean) Safety rules used in this class: - The file path is never hardcoded. The user types it, and the JDBC connection string is built by joining "jdbc:sqlite:" and that path. - Every value typed by the user goes into the SQL as a ? parameter in a PreparedStatement, never joined into the SQL text. - Every method catches SQLException and returns a value (false, null, an empty list or -1.0) with a message in getLastError(), so a database problem can never crash the program.

    • WorkoutDatabase

      public WorkoutDatabase()
      Creates a WorkoutDatabase that is not connected yet. Call connect with the path of a SQLite file before using any other method.

  • Method Details

    • connect

      public boolean connect(String filePath)
      Opens the SQLite database file at the path the user typed. The file must already exist (a missing file is never created), must be a real SQLite file, and must have the workouts table. If anything is wrong the old connection (if there was one) stays open and getLastError() explains the problem.
      Parameters:
      filePath - the path typed by the user (blank or quoted paths are handled)
      Returns:
      true if the database was opened, false if there was a problem

    • disconnect

      public boolean disconnect()
      Closes the database connection.
      Returns:
      true if a connection was closed, false if there was none

    • isConnected

      public boolean isConnected()
      Checks whether a database is open right now.
      Returns:
      true if connected

    • insertWorkout

      public boolean insertWorkout(Workout workout)
      Adds a workout to the database (INSERT).
      Parameters:
      workout - the workout to add
      Returns:
      true if it was added, false if it was null, the ID already exists, or there was a database problem

    • deleteWorkout

      public boolean deleteWorkout(int id)
      Deletes the workout with the given ID (DELETE).
      Parameters:
      id - the ID to delete
      Returns:
      true if a workout was deleted, false if the ID was not found or there was a database problem

    • updateWorkout

      public boolean updateWorkout(int id, String field, String newValue)
      Changes one field of one workout (UPDATE). The new value is checked by the validator again, so bad data can never reach the database.
      Parameters:
      id - the ID of the workout to change
      field - one of: name, duration, weight, met, completed
      newValue - the new value as text
      Returns:
      true if the workout was updated, false if the ID, field or value was bad or there was a database problem

    • selectAllWorkouts

      public List<Workout> selectAllWorkouts()
      Reads every workout from the database (SELECT), sorted by ID. Rows with invalid data (for example edited by hand outside the program) are skipped and counted in getSkippedRows().
      Returns:
      the workouts, or an empty list if there are none or there was a problem

      Returns:
      the Workout, or null if it was not found (or there was a problem, see getLastError())

    • calculateCalories

      public double calculateCalories(int id)
      Custom action: calculates the calories burned for a workout stored in the database. Formula: MET x weight in kilograms x duration in hours.
      Parameters:
      id - the ID of the workout
      Returns:
      the calories burned, or -1.0 if the workout was not found
